title: Withheld renders stayed publicly downloadable: /media/photos/<id> served any photo id, purged ones included
evidence: MediaController#photo served bytes for ANY photo id and the ids are sequential behind the Cloudflare tunnel, so /media/photos/1..N is enumerable. A post purged by the NSFW gate deletes only the POST row: 13 such purges (action=nsfw_purge, scores 0.93-0.9999) left the Photo row and its bytes intact. Measured 2026-09-23 through the tunnel: GET /media/photos/241 -> 200 and /media/photos/228 -> 200 (both purged), plus 38 further renders of the persona that never became a post at all (51 unlinked Sarah photos: 28 from the 2026-05-28 batch, 10 from 2026-08, 13 purged; 51/51 resolve to a file on disk).

notes.note: FIXED in 60dd50b: MediaController#photo now serves a photo only while a post still references it (404 otherwise). The rule is one-sided on purpose -- the publishing path always builds the URL from a post that already exists (Scheduling::Commands::GeneratePublicPhotoUrl, from schedule_post.rb / scheduled_posting.rake) and captioning base64s the local file, so no publish can be broken, while a render no post references has no publishing consumer to lose. VERIFIED: spec/requests/media_spec.rb new (4 examples incl. the purged-post case), full spec/requests + spec/models = 67 examples / 0 failures; live through the tunnel after the fix -- 241/228 (purged) and 124/308 (unlinked) now 404, while 345/330 (publishable) and 9 (posted) still 200, and GeneratePublicPhotoUrl still returns https://carnival.pi216.ai/media/photos/345 for the next scheduled post (clock 17:35Z). DECISION recorded with it: the 51 unlinked Sarah renders are NOT a spare-content reserve that could cover the render outage -- 13 are NSFW-purged (that is why they have no post) and the other 38 are from a superseded render era (28 from the 2026-05-28 bulk batch, 10 strays from 2026-08), so publishing them would put unvetted/off-era imagery on the public feed. No GPU-free supply lever exists; the queue's own runway (dry_out) is the constraint.

NARROWED by B5 (PRD 0007, ticket #111): the serving rule is now the post's SELECTION STATE, not merely 'a post references it.' MediaController#photo/#reel serve a post's bytes only while Scheduling::Post#selection_state is :published (posted / provider post id) or :queued (unpublished with a publish slot); a HELD post (a gate cleared scheduled_at AND optimal_time_calculated, keeping the row), a never-queued post, a failed post, a purged post (row deleted), and a render no post references all 404 (not 403). Nothing is deleted -- held/flagged bytes stay on disk and in the corpus for re-valuation (A1). A held post is recognised by its CLEARED CLOCKS, keeping the rule inside the scheduling pack. State->HTTP matrix: spec/requests/media_spec.rb (31 examples) + spec/models/scheduling/post_selection_state_spec.rb (15 examples); full bin/verify green (917 examples / 0 failures).
